transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep forgetting small things I usually manage fine—like returning phone calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s not huge things, but it’s been happening enough that it’s starting to worry me.
Can you tell me when you first started noticing these memory lapses, and how long this has been going on?

I started really noticing it after I began my evening certificate program. That was about 15 months ago. I mean, I’ve always had to work a little to stay organized, but since then it’s been noticeably harder to keep up with things.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually anxious, worried, or on edge over these past several months?
Not really, no. I mean, I get frustrated when I realize I forgot something, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually anxious or on edge.
Over the past several months, have you noticed a persistent low mood or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve been annoyed with myself when I forget things, but I haven’t felt persistently down, and I still enjoy the things I usually like.
Thinking back to your childhood and early adulthood, did you have similar struggles with forgetfulness, staying organized, or maintaining focus before this recent 15-month period?

Yes, looking back, I guess it was there when I was a kid too. In elementary school I was always forgetting permission slips, losing homework somewhere in my backpack, things like that. My mom or my teacher would have to remind me step by step to finish projects, or I just wouldn’t get them done right.

Between childhood and now, would you say these attention and organization difficulties have caused ongoing problems in multiple areas of your life—like school, work, and home—fairly continuously, or did they mostly go away for a while before coming back recently?

I’d say it’s been pretty ongoing, not like it went away completely. I’ve managed to get by, but it has caused problems in different areas. In school I missed deadlines, and now at work I’ll miss small follow-ups often enough that I worry people notice. I’m concerned it could hurt my reputation or my chances of moving into an Office Manager role.
Do you often feel restless, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively in daily situations?

I wouldn’t say I’m really impulsive or interrupting people a lot. But I do get fidgety, especially if I have to sit for a long time. Like in longer classes, I’ll catch myself clicking my pen, bouncing my foot, or shifting around in the chair even when I’m trying to sit still and pay attention.

Right now, outside of work and your certificate program, do these forgetfulness or organization issues also cause problems for you at home—like with chores, bills, or keeping track of personal responsibilities?

Yes, it does. That’s actually part of what made me finally ask for help. I keep forgetting little things I usually handle, like returning calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s not huge things every day, but it happens enough that it’s becoming a problem.
